SIDEWALK CAFE ORDINANCE FOR TOWN OF PINE MOUNTAIN, GEORGIA 1-10-1. Definitions.

- (a) Sidewalk Cafe. “Sidewalk Cafe” shall mean the location and use of tables and chairs and other associated equipment and furnishings on the public sidewalk and operated as an extension of a licensed restaurant in the Town of Pine Mountain, Georgia, and which sidewalk cafe shall be an incidental activity of the restaurant.

- (b) Clerk. The term “Clerk” shall mean the Town Clerk of the Town of Pine Mountain, Georgia, or his/her designee.

1-10-2. Permits.

No person shall operate a sidewalk cafe in Pine Mountain, Georgia, without a permit issued by the Clerk. Such permit shall be renewed annually at the time to be designated by the Clerk.

1-10-3. Applications.

Any person desiring to operate a sidewalk cafe in the Town of Pine Mountain, Georgia, shall submit an application on a form prescribed by the Clerk, to the Clerk describing the name of the restaurant, the name of the owner of the restaurant, the name of the individual applying for the permit, the exact number of tables and chairs that will be used, a description of the divider that will be utilized, and any other such information which the Clerk deems appropriate to describe fully the planned operation. A non-refundable administrative processing fee of $50.00, payable to the Town of Pine Mountain, Georgia, shall be paid at the time the application is submitted.

1-10-4. Permit Fees,

The annual fee for a permit to operate a sidewalk cafe in the Town of Pine Mountain, Georgia, shall be $50.00 plus an additional $10.00 for each table. No more than two (2) chairs shall be permitted at any one table.

1-10-5. Regulations Generally.

Except as otherwise provided in Section 1-10-6 herein, a sidewalk cafe operating in the Town of Pine Mountain, Georgia, shall comply with the following regulations:

- (1) Limitations on area. The area in which a sidewalk cafe is operated shall abut the outside front wall of the restaurant of which it is an extension and shall not extend parallel in either direction beyond the outside front wall of the restaurant. The area permitted for a sidewalk cafe shall not extend more than four (4) feet perpendicular from the outside wall of the restaurant; however, a minimum of four (4) feet shall be provided at all times for continuous, unobstructed pedestrian traffic on the sidewalk between the sidewalk cafe area and curb or nearest obstacle.

- (2) __ Divider. The area in which the sidewalk cafe is located shall be separated from the remaining sidewalk area by a removable divider constructed from a sturdy material such as wrought iron, metal or wood posts and chain, or other such materials as the Clerk may deem safe and appropriate to the location. Such divider shall not be less than three (3) feet nor more than four (4) feet in height. All tables and chairs and other associated equipment or furnishings shall be located totally within the limits of the divider.

- (3) Sanitation. A covered trash container of at least 32 gallons capacity, containing a disposable plastic liner or bag, shall be provided within each sidewalk cafe area and shall be emptied as often as necessary to prevent overflow or other unsanitary conditions. It shall be the responsibility and duty of the restaurant to which the sidewalk cafe permit is issued to maintain such an area and all equipment and furnishings in such conditions so as to be clean, sanitary and safe at all times.

- (4) Removal of furnishings. All tables, chairs, trash containers, dividers and other associated equipment or furnishings of a sidewalk cafe shall be removed from the public sidewalk area at the close of business every day.

- (5) Suspension or modification of operations. The Clerk shall have the authority to require any sidewalk cafe operating in an area created by this section to suspend operation and clear such area, or to move or modify a location or operation of the sidewalk cafe, during any permitted special event occurring within the Town of Pine Mountain, Georgia.

1-10-6. Open Containers,

- (a) “Open container” defined. The term “open container,” as used in this chapter means any bottle, can, glass, cup or other vessel which contains an alcoholic beverage not in its original container. The term “open container” shall also mean the original container of an alcoholic beverage and which contains an alcoholic beverage on which the seal has been broken or which is otherwise ready for consumption.

- (b) Application to sidewalk cafes. The prohibition on open containers shall not apply to patrons of a sidewalk cafe as defines in the applicable zoning ordinances, if such establishment is otherwise licensed to sell alcoholic beverages under the applicable laws and ordinances in Pine Mountain, Georgia.

- (c) Posting of notice by establishments. All licensed alcohol establishments are hereby required to post in a conspicuous location inside such establishment a notice informing patrons that open containers are prohibited on areas outside the sidewalk cafe, as defined in 1-10-1 of this title.

1-10-7. Indemnification.

Before any permit is issued pursuant to this ordinance, every applicant for a permit or any business seeking a permit shall in writing, on a form provided by the Clerk, agree to defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Town of Pine Mountain, Georgia, and their respective agents, employees and officers from any and all liability, claims, damages, actions and causes of actions of whatsoever kind or nature for any loss, damage or injury to persons, including death or damage to property, regardless of how arising and however caused arising out of the operation of any sidewalk cafe as contemplated by this ordinance.

1-10-8. Liability Insurance.
1:
Each applicant and any business associated with each applicant shall have in force and effect at the time of application for a permit, and shall maintain at all times the permit is in effect, a policy or policies of insurance issued by an insurance company or companies authorized to do business in the State of Georgia in the form generally known as comprehensive general liability insurance insuring applicant and applicant’s business. Before any permit is issued to applicant, applicant shall require a certificate of insurance to be issued by applicant’s insurance company listing the Mayor and Council of the Town of Pine Mountain, Georgia, as an additional insured on each policy or policies. Such policy or policies shall be written with no less than Two Million Dollars ($2,000,000.00) in coverage. Applicant shall provide a copy of each policy in effect, or a certificate evidencing the same, as a condition precedent to the issuance of any permit under this ordinance. Applicant shall be responsible for making certain that all insurance coverage contemplated by this ordinance shall remain in full force and effect for the entire time that the applicant maintains a permit.

ADOPTED BY THE TOWN OF PINE MOUNTAIN COUNCIL ON JANUARY 12, 2004.

Mayor Joe D Teel, Jr.

Attest: Betsy Chapman
